header.intro: A collection of experiments to touch, observe, and understand Angular in motion. Each circuit turns a code concept into something you can watch happening.

list.title: Choose an experiment
list.intro: Each page investigates one idea at a time. You interact with the example, follow the interface reaction, and then visit the code responsible for the movement.

available.title: Components in conversation
available.description: Send a value from the parent component to the child, choose a reply, and watch the event find its way back.

header.intro: Send a value across the boundary between parent and child. Then follow the reply returning as an event and see the code involved in each passage.

exhibit.title: Parent, child, and the path back
exhibit.intro: The parent holds the message and Angular carries it to the child. The child chooses a reply and emits a return event. You trigger the flow; the interface records each passage.

guide.title: Send the message through the circuit

parent.title: The parent sends
parent.text: Write a message or use the example.

child.title: The child chooses
child.text: Read the received value and select a reply.

return.title: The parent receives

parent.title: The sender
parent.label: Message for the child component
parent.hint: Not sure what to write? Start with a ready-made message.
parent.inputNote: is a property binding: it carries the value from the parent to the child's input.

child.title: The receiver
child.waiting: The child is still waiting for a value from the parent.
child.reply: Choose a reply from the child
child.outputNote: creates an output through which the child emits an event to its container.

responses.acknowledge: Child: message received. The complete value arrived.
responses.measure: Child: I processed the value. It contains {{ count }} characters.

timeline.title: What happened beneath the interface
timeline.note: This panel does not receive clicks. It only records, in order, what your actions trigger in the circuit above.
timeline.parentState: The parent updates the value stored in its state.
timeline.binding: Angular evaluates the expression bound to the message property.
timeline.childInput: The child receives the new value through its @Input.
timeline.childOutput: When clicked, the child emits an event through @Output.
timeline.parentHandler: The parent handles the event and updates its interface again.

parent.title: 1. The parent prepares and sends the value
parent.description: Signals hold the message while the send method updates the value that will be delivered to the child.

binding.title: 2. The template creates the connection
binding.description: Property binding sends the value through [message]. Event binding listens for the reply through (reply).

child.title: 3. The child receives and prepares a reply
child.description: @Input creates the child's entry point. @Output and EventEmitter create the path back to the parent component.

return.title: 4. The parent handles the reply
return.description: The method receives the object emitted by the child, stores the reply in a Signal, and advances the visual log.

action.title: What do you do?
action.text: Write a message, send it to the child, and ask it to reply. Each action changes the visible stage of the experiment.

angular.title: What does Angular notice?
angular.text: It detects the change, reevaluates the connection between components, and updates only the interface fragments that depend on those values.

code.title: What moves in the code?
code.text: The value moves down from parent to child through @Input. The event returns from child to parent through @Output and EventEmitter.
